MVBU Core S7 Class Architecture

Source: R/S7-class.R
MVBU-core-classes.Rd

The MVBeliefUpdatr S7 organizes model objects around an explicit compositional structure. These classes define the canonical S7 API; any older list/data-frame-style inputs are supported only through transitional compatibility methods and should be phased out over time.

Constructs a cognitive model binding a category representation template to model-level decision and uncertainty parameters.

Usage

new_cognitive_model(
  category_template = NULL,
  decision_rule = "sampling",
  category_prior = NULL,
  lapse_rate = 0,
  lapse_bias = NULL,
  Sigma_noise = NULL,
  noise_treatment = .infer_noise_treatment(Sigma_noise),
  lapse_treatment = .infer_lapse_treatment(lapse_rate),
  metadata = list()
)

Arguments

metadata

Optional list of metadata. Defaults to list().

category_template

An MVBU_CategoryRepresentationTemplate object containing category representations.

decision_rule

Categorization decision rule: "sampling", "criterion", or "proportional". Defaults to "sampling".

category_prior

Optional numeric vector of prior category probabilities summing to 1. Defaults to equal priors.

lapse_rate

Numeric scalar lapse probability in [0, 1]. Defaults to 0.

lapse_bias

Optional numeric vector of lapse category probabilities summing to 1. Defaults to uniform bias across categories.

Sigma_noise

Optional perceptual/measurement noise covariance matrix or scalar variance. Defaults to NULL.

noise_treatment

Treatment of perceptual noise during evaluation and updating: "no_noise", "sample", or "marginalize".

  • "no_noise": No perceptual noise is applied to input cues, and no noise is assumed during categorization.

  • "sample": Simulates sensory noise on a specific observation. Noise drawn from \(\mathcal{N}(0, \Sigma_{\text{noise}})\) is added to input cues (and projected into composite cue space in early integration), and the observer accounts for their own noise uncertainty during categorization by adding \(\Sigma_{\text{noise}}\) to their likelihood scale.

  • "marginalize": Evaluates categorization in the limit across infinitely many noisy encounters (expected consequences). No noise is sampled onto the input stimulus, but \(\Sigma_{\text{noise}}\) is added to the category covariance scale.

Defaults to .infer_noise_treatment(Sigma_noise): "marginalize" if noise is present, "no_noise" otherwise.

lapse_treatment

Treatment of attentional lapses during evaluation and updating: "no_lapses", "sample", or "marginalize".

  • "no_lapses": Lapses are ignored; categorization and updating reflect pure normative evidence evaluation (even if lapse_rate > 0).

  • "sample": Simulates stochastic attentional lapses on individual observations. With probability lapse_rate, a lapse occurs: during categorization, the posterior is replaced by lapse_bias; during updating, the lapsing observation is treated as uninformative.

  • "marginalize": Evaluates categorization in the limit across infinitely many encounters (expected response probabilities). The category posterior is the mixture \((1 - \lambda) p(c \mid x) + \lambda b_c\), and evidence during updating is downweighted by \(1 - \lambda\).

Defaults to .infer_lapse_treatment(lapse_rate): "marginalize" if lapse_rate > 0, "no_lapses" otherwise.

Value

An MVBU_CognitiveModel object.

Details

  • MVBU_CategoryRepresentation defines the structure for one category-level representational object. This could be a uni- or multivariate Gaussian, a mixture of Gaussians, or an exemplar-based representation.

  • MVBU_CategoryRepresentationTemplate collects one or more category-representation objects into a validated set used by a model. This corresponds to the notion of "templates" in e.g., (Nearey and Assmann 2007) .

  • MVBU_CognitiveModel combines category-template structure with model-level decision behavior (decision_rule, category_prior, lapse_rate, lapse_bias).

Family-level semantics are layered on top of these base classes. Ideal observer/adaptor pairings follow:

  • UVG_IdealObserver UVG <-> NIX_IdealAdaptor NIX

  • MUVG_IdealObserver MUVG <-> MNIX_IdealAdaptor MNIX

  • MVG_IdealObserver MVG <-> NIW_IdealAdaptor NIW

while Exemplar_Model EXEMPLAR is treated as a standalone family.

MVBU_Object

Root S7 base class for MVBeliefUpdatr objects.

MVBU_CategoryRepresentation

Abstract category-level representational class.

Expected properties:

  • category_labels: one or more category labels associated with the object.

  • cue_labels: one or more cue-dimension labels.

  • category_likelihood_function: family-specific likelihood function

MVBU_CategoryRepresentationTemplate

Container class for per-category representation objects.

Expected properties:

  • representations: list of objects inheriting from MVBU_CategoryRepresentation.

  • metadata: optional template-level metadata.

Validators enforce at least one representation and (if named) unique, non-empty representation names.

MVBU_CognitiveModel

Abstract model class binding a category-representation template to model-level decision and uncertainty parameters.

Expected properties:

  • category_template: MVBU_CategoryRepresentationTemplate.

  • category_posterior_functions: named list of treatment-specific posterior functions.

  • decision_rule: scalar character rule label.

  • category_prior: numeric probability vector over represented categories.

  • lapse_behavior: list bundling attentional lapse parameters: lapse_rate (scalar probability in [0, 1]), lapse_bias (vector of lapse response probabilities across categories), and lapse_treatment ("no_lapses", "sample", or "marginalize").

  • noise_behavior: list bundling perceptual noise parameters: Sigma_noise (perceptual noise covariance matrix) and noise_treatment ("no_noise", "sample", or "marginalize"). Sigma_noise is stored as a square matrix and may be supplied as a vector (converted to a diagonal matrix) or as a matrix.

  • metadata: optional model metadata.

References

Nearey TM, Assmann PF (2007). “Probabilistic 'sliding template' models for indirect vowel normalization.” In Solé M, Beddor PS, Ohala M (eds.), Experimental Approaches to Phonology, 246–269. Oxford University Press, Oxford.

Xie X, Jaeger TF, Kurumada C (2023). “What we do (not) know about the mechanisms underlying adaptive speech perception: A computational framework and review.” Cortex, 166, 377–424.

Xie, X., Jaeger, T. F., & Kurumada, C. (2021). What we do (not) know about the mechanisms underlying adaptive speech perception: A computational review.
